les: Al daardie water, en so min om te drink

items.bewering: Nie alle water op die aarde is dieselfde nie. Daar is twee soorte water: soutwater en varswater.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Saline Water and Salinity' (usgs.gov): freshwater is less than 1 000 ppm dissolved salts, and everything above that is graded as saline (slightly, moderately, highly; ocean about 35 000 ppm). So the fresh/salt split is the USGS's own two-way classification. Brackish water, for example in estuaries (Wikipedia 'Brackish water': 0.5 to 30 g/L), falls inside USGS's saline grades rather than forming a third kind, so the binary holds. Checked fresh this round.

items.bewering: Soutwater bevat baie sout, en ons vind dit in die oseane.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': ocean water holds about 35 000 ppm of salt (about 35 g per litre). USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?': oceans, seas and bays hold 96.5% of all water, and it is saline. The sentence does not say salt water is found ONLY in the oceans.

items.bewering: Mense kan nie soutwater drink nie
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': 'Humans cannot drink saline water.' USGS Water Q&A 'Why can't people drink seawater?' and NOAA, quoted in secondary sources: the kidneys can only make urine less salty than blood, and seawater is about three times saltier than blood, so drinking it dehydrates the body.

items.bewering: en die meeste diere en plante op land ook nie.
items.bron: Plants: Flowers and Colmer 2015 (PMC4332615) put plants that can grow and reproduce with repeated exposure to seawater at under 0.2% of species. Glenn, Brown and Blumwald 1999 (UC Davis) put halophytes at about 2% of land plant species. Animals: the exceptions in the sources are seabirds with salt glands (albatrosses, penguins, gulls) and marine mammals, not ordinary land animals. 'Die meeste' is the right quantifier: the sentence does not say every one.

items.bewering: Varswater is die water wat ons elke dag drink en waarmee ons kos maak en was.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': freshwater (under 1 000 ppm) is the water fit for drinking, and saline water cannot be drunk. Household drinking, cooking and washing water is fresh water. WHO sodium and chloride fact sheets: typical drinking water carries under 20 mg/L sodium.

items.bewering: Boere lei ook hulle gewasse met varswater nat.
items.bron: Department of Water and Sanitation, Deputy Minister's speaking notes to the Agri SA colloquium, 2019 (dws.gov.za), citing the National Water Resources Strategy 2: agriculture uses about 60% of South Africa's water, mostly for irrigation. GCIS SA Yearbook, Water and Sanitation chapter: agriculture is 61%. That is fresh surface water and groundwater. Seawater kills most crops (see the plant item above).

items.bewering: Varswater bevat baie min sout. Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout daarin maar gewoonlik te min om dit te proe.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': fresh water is under 1 000 ppm dissolved salts, so it is not salt-free. WHO chloride fact sheet: the taste threshold for sodium chloride is about 200 to 300 mg/L. WHO sodium fact sheet: drinking water usually holds under 20 mg/L sodium. Most fresh water is therefore below the taste threshold, though some fresh water can be tasted, and 'gewoonlik' covers that.

items.bewering: Ons vind varswater in riviere en strome, in die meeste mere en die meeste vleilande.
items.bron: Rivers: USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?' lists river water as fresh. Lakes: freshwater lakes outnumber saline lakes by count (Limnetica 41(2), 2022: most lakes lie in boreal and Arctic regions). By VOLUME the split is close to even, about 52% fresh to 48% saline (USGS table), and the Caspian Sea holds about 91% of the saline lake water. 'Die meeste mere' is true by count and, narrowly, by volume. Wetlands: Davidson et al., Marine and Freshwater Research (CSIRO, MF17019): inland wetlands are about 93% of continental wetland area and coastal ones about 7%. So 'die meeste vleilande' holds. Both 'die meeste' qualifiers are correct, and they should not be widened to 'alle'.

items.bewering: Daar is ook varswater in ys en onder die grond.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?': ice caps, glaciers and permanent snow hold 68.7% of all fresh water. Fresh groundwater holds 30.1%. Not all groundwater is fresh (0.93% of all water is saline groundwater), but the sentence only says there IS fresh water underground.

items.bewering: Die meeste van die aarde se water lê in die oseane, en daardie water is sout.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?': oceans, seas and bays hold 96.54% of all Earth's water, and it is saline.

items.bewering: Van al die water op aarde is net 'n klein deel varswater wat mense kan gebruik.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?': fresh water is about 2.5% of all water, and 68.7% of that is locked in ice. True under both readings of the sentence: a small share is fresh, and a still smaller share is fresh water people can reach.

items.bewering: Varswater is dus baie skaarser as soutwater.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's Water?': about 2.5% of all water is fresh and about 97.5% is saline (oceans 96.54% plus saline groundwater and saline lakes).

items.bewering: 'n Natuurlike hulpbron is iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Natural resource': resources drawn from nature and used with few modifications. Arizona Geographic Alliance (geoalliance.asu.edu): a natural material becomes a resource once people value and use it. Both support the definition, including its 'mense gebruik' part.

items.bewering: Die hout van bome is 'n natuurlike hulpbron, en so is die grond waarin boere kos kweek.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Natural resource': the standard list includes water, land, minerals, vegetation and wildlife. The US federal legal definition (uslegal.com) lists vegetation, water, air and soils. Wood (vegetation) and soil both appear in these lists.

items.bewering: Water is een van die belangrikste natuurlike hulpbronne wat ons het.
items.bron: This is the softened form ('een van die'), which is defensible. NASA Astrobiology, 'Why is water so important for life?': every known life form depends on water. DWS and the GCIS SA Yearbook: water supports agriculture, which uses about 60% of it, plus municipalities, mining and energy. The lesson does not call water the MOST important resource, and it should not.

items.bewering: Elke mens, dier en plant het water nodig om te lewe.
items.bron: NASA Astrobiology, 'What does life need for survival?': all living things we know of need water to stay alive, and even desert cacti need some. American Museum of Natural History, OLogy, 'What is water?': all living things, from cyanobacteria to blue whales, need water to survive. A universal claim, but one the sources state universally.

items.bewering: Jy het al gesien hoe nat wasgoed aan die draad in die son droog word. Die water in die klere verdwyn nie sommer nie. Die son maak die water warm, en van die water verander in waterdamp.
items.bron: Mapping checked: drying washing stands for evaporation, and the lesson carries it over to rivers, dams, soil and the sea. The mapping holds. USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': evaporation happens when energy (heat) breaks the bonds holding water molecules together. The sentence names the sun as the heat source in the sunlit case. It does not say water evaporates ONLY in the sun, so a learner who sees washing dry in the shade meets nothing false. 'Van die water' (not all of it at once) is accurate.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp styg op in die lug, maar jy kan dit nie sien nie. Ons noem hierdie verandering verdamping.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Water vapor': water vapour is transparent and less dense than dry air, and warm moist air rises. USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': water evaporates into water vapour and rises into the sky to become part of a cloud. Dictionary.com, 'vapor': steam as a gas is invisible, and the visible part is condensed droplets. Liquid to vapour is the definition of evaporation (USGS).

items.bewering: Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en die see.
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': about 90% of the moisture in the atmosphere evaporated from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers. Soil evaporation is a recognised part of evapotranspiration (USGS Water Science School, evapotranspiration topic). Dams are open water bodies like lakes.

items.bewering: Die son maak ook die seewater warm, en van daardie water verdamp. Die sout kan nie saam met die waterdamp opstyg nie en bly in die see agter.
items.bron: EarthDate, 'How Earth Makes Fresh Water' (earthdate.org, University of Texas Bureau of Economic Geology): when water changes from liquid to gas it leaves salt and other impurities behind, and the water cycle constantly desalinates seawater. USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': table salt is produced by evaporating saline water in ponds.

items.bewering: Jy kan dit self sien as jy 'n bakkie soutwater in die son laat staan. Na 'n ruk is die water weg en lê daar 'n wit lagie sout in die bakkie.
items.bron: Mapping checked: a bowl of salt water stands for the sea, and the residue shows the salt stays behind. The mapping holds for the one thing it is used to show. The lesson does not draw the false further step that the sea dries out. Wikipedia 'Salt evaporation pond': seawater left in shallow ponds in the sun evaporates and leaves salt to harvest. The historical Egyptian method left salt behind on posts. 'Na 'n ruk' is honest about the time this takes, which can be several days.

items.bewering: Daarom bevat die waterdamp uit die see geen sout nie.
items.bron: EarthDate 'How Earth Makes Fresh Water', and the meteorologist explanations in WGN 'Ask Tom Why' and the AJC: salt is dissolved in seawater, not bonded to the water, so only water molecules leave as vapour. Sea-spray particles do carry salt into the air, but they are aerosol, not water vapour, so the sentence as worded (about the VAPOUR) is true.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp vorm later wolke wat reën gee.
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': water vapour rises to become part of a cloud, and it condenses when saturated air cools. The cooling step is left out, but nothing false is said.

items.bewering: So kom baie van ons varswater eintlik uit die sout see.
items.bron: HESS 27, 481 (2023, Copernicus): about 42% of land precipitation comes from ocean evaporation. Discussion papers in ACP put it at 35 to 40% or more. USGS water flux tables give about 46 000 km³ a year of ocean-to-land transport against about 110 600 km³ of land precipitation. 'Baie' (much, not most) is the right quantifier. 'Die meeste' would be contestable, because of land recycling.

items.bewering: soutwater: Water wat baie sout bevat, soos die water in die oseane.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': ocean water holds about 35 000 ppm. The definition matches the study block 'Twee soorte water'. Read alone, it is true. 'Soos' introduces an example, not an exhaustive list.

items.bewering: varswater: Water wat baie min sout bevat, soos die water in riviere en die meeste mere.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': freshwater is under 1 000 ppm, so it has very little salt but not none. 'Die meeste mere' holds by count (Limnetica 2022), and narrowly by volume (USGS table, about 52% fresh). Read alone, it is true. The qualifier on lakes matches the study block, so the two do not disagree.

items.bewering: natuurlike hulpbron: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Natural resource' and the Arizona Geographic Alliance, as for the study-block definition. The glossary wording is identical to the study block's, so they agree.

opsomming: Every claim was checked against the web this round, nothing was carried forward, and all 27 items are confirmed. The 'die meeste' qualifiers on lakes, wetlands and land animals and plants, the 'baie' on fresh water coming from the sea, and the 'een van die belangrikste' on water are the correct strength and must not be widened; 'twee soorte water' holds because the USGS itself splits water into fresh (under 1 000 ppm) and saline, with brackish water falling inside the saline grades.
